editorial:
Imagine walking into a dusty old London museum where the statues look way too real. You are following a group of people trying to sell the place, but they quickly realize they are not alone. The vibe is creepy and mysterious, with scary figures like Jack the Ripper staring at you from every corner. It feels like a classic whodunit where you are constantly guessing who the killer is and why they are turning people into wax art. You will feel the tension build as the characters get trapped in this weird gallery of horrors.

What really works here is the slow build-up and the cool set design. The acting is solid for the time, and the twists keep you on your toes. While some parts feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you love old-school mystery movies, you should definitely check this one out. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend when you want something spooky but not too modern.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the museum owner is the killer. He wants to keep his museum famous, so he kills people and covers them in wax to make them look like historical figures. In the end, the hero finds the secret room where the victims are hidden. After a tense struggle, the killer ends up becoming a wax statue himself. The police arrive, and the nightmare finally ends with the museum closing down for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old horror movies and classic murder mysteries.
